title: A dominating DVR in a prescribed finitely generated field extension
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is a local integral domain and not a field: $R
e0$, it has no zero divisors, and it has a unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R
e0$. Let $K\subseteq L$ be fields [def-weil-field], with $R\subseteq K$ and with every element of $K$ a quotient $r/s$ for $r,s\in R$, $s
e0$ (so $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$). Assume $L/K$ is finitely generated as a field extension: $L=K(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ for finitely many $a_i\in L$, where this denotes the smallest subfield containing $K$ and the $a_i$. Then there is a discrete valuation subring $A\subseteq L$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] containing $R$ such that every element of $L$ is a quotient of elements of $A$ and $\mathfrak m_A\cap R=\mathfrak m_R$. Here $\mathfrak m_A$ is the unique maximal ideal of $A$.

source.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr (full statement, including a finitely generated extension L/K).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-polynomial-origin-finite-field-reduction] to $R\subseteq K\subseteq L$. It gives $R\subseteq B\subseteq K_0\subseteq L$ with $B$ a nonfield Noetherian local domain, $\operatorname{Frac}(B)=K_0$, $\mathfrak m_B\cap R=\mathfrak m_R$, and $[L:K_0]<\infty$. All its hypotheses are exactly the hypotheses on $R,K,L$.

source.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, first paragraph; Fields Tags 030F (fields-lemma-transcendence-degree) and 09GH (fields-lemma-algebraic-finitely-generated).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-local-domain-birational-dimension-one] with input ring $B$ and ambient field $K_0$, and call its output subring $D$. Step 1 supplies its nonfield Noetherian local domain and fraction-field hypotheses. Thus $B\subseteq D\subseteq K_0$, $D$ is a Noetherian local integral domain of dimension $1$, $\operatorname{Frac}(D)=K_0$ for this inclusion, and $\mathfrak m_D\cap B=\mathfrak m_B$. Choose $0\ne t\in\mathfrak m_R$; injectivity and the two contractions put this same nonzero element in $\mathfrak m_B$ and $\mathfrak m_D$. In particular $\mathfrak m_D\ne0$, and $\mathfrak m_D\cap R=\mathfrak m_R$.

source.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, second paragraph; Tag 00P8, algebra-lemma-dominate-by-dimension-1.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-normalization-local-dvr] with its $D,K,L$ equal to $D,K_0,L$. Step 2 supplies the nonzero Noetherian local domain of dimension $1$, its nonzero maximal ideal, and its prescribed fraction field; step 1 supplies $[L:K_0]<\infty$. The lemma gives the integral closure $C\subseteq L$, a prime $\mathfrak q$ above $\mathfrak m_D$, and the subring $A=\{c/s\in L:c,s\in C,\ s\notin\mathfrak q\}$ identified with $C_{\mathfrak q}$. It states that this $A$ is a DVR containing $D$, has fraction field $L$, and satisfies $\mathfrak m_A\cap C=\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak m_A\cap D=\mathfrak m_D$.

source.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, final paragraph, normalization and lying over; Tag 09IG, algebra-lemma-integral-closure-Dedekind; the fraction-field clause of normalization in a finite extension.

proof.text: The inclusions give $R\subseteq B\subseteq D\subseteq C\subseteq A\subseteq L$, and $\mathfrak m_A\cap R=(\mathfrak m_A\cap D)\cap R=\mathfrak m_D\cap R=\mathfrak m_R$. Since $\operatorname{Frac}(A)=L$ for this inclusion, each element of $L$ is a quotient of elements of this $A$. These are exactly all the required clauses.

source.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, final sentence: domination; contraction through a prime localization.

proof_origin.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, all three paragraphs, using the existing Tag 09IG normalization package for its last paragraph.
